arguments.value: DGT and Dolphin agreed that Dolphin would outsource photo-editing work for DGT. The agreement has no stated overall term or duration, but it includes a 90-day payment commitment after successful beta testing and allows either party to terminate for a material breach if the breach is not cured after written notice within the stated cure period. DGT must pay Dolphin $10,000 for beta testing and bandwidth testing, in two $5,000 installments, one on the agreement date and one 30 days later. If beta testing is successful, DGT must then pay the greater of $5,000 for each 30-day period of photo-editing work for 90 days or at least 3,300 photos per 30-day period for 90 days at $1.50 per completed photo. Dolphin must complete work within 14 days of receiving the original files and meet DGT’s standards. Dolphin charges $1.50 per completed photo, but the price can be renegotiated with written notice. If annual volume reaches 50,000 photos, Dolphin may be required to provide exclusive photo-editing services at DGT’s option. Dolphin may not copy or reproduce the photos without permission, must keep records and provide yearly reports, and must keep information confidential. Dolphin must also indemnify DGT for claims related to the work, while DGT’s liability is limited and consequential damages are excluded. The agreement is governed by Nevada law, disputes go to a single arbitrator under Nevada arbitration law in English, and the contract includes standard terms such as force majeure and inspection rights.
